decisions.summary: Reads recorded by a pytest plugin make test-file loads, L7R_TEST_DEPS=record by default; an audit hook notes files opened and directories listed under the repository
decisions.why: FR-013's 'records what it read - the files it opened and the directories it listed'. Premise, not checked here: the clone's ordinary tooling-test runs must load the plugin, or only hand-run make test-file passes are recorded and reuse reaches less than the GM's 'skip suites the clone already passed'.

decisions.summary: A compiled module read (__pycache__/*.pyc) stands for its source
decisions.why: The .pyc is derived from the source; keying by the source is keying by what was read, by content.

decisions.summary: Every Python child imports a recording sitecustomize on PYTHONPATH (system sitecustomize first), reads written as first seen
decisions.why: FR-013's 'in every Python process it started'; writing as first seen keeps a killed child's reads.

decisions.summary: Opaque predicate: git or make started with cwd in the repository is deemed NOT on the repository when it names any path outside the repository
decisions.why: FR-013: a file that started any other program against the repository is always run, since what that program read is not known. The clause 'and naming no path outside the repository' exempts git/make commands run from the repository that read it while naming an outside path - git worktree add /tmp/base HEAD (the project's own baseline recipe), git clone <repo> /tmp/x, git archive -o /tmp/x.tar HEAD - so a test whose outcome rests on what those read is skipped on changed inputs, the false skip the 'always run' rule exists to prevent. Not impossible, not implied by the request, and the literal rule does not defeat the purpose: git on a tmp fixture repo is already excluded by the cwd/-C test alone. Should read: opaque unless the program's cwd (and any -C) is outside the repository AND no argument names a path inside it; Python children isolated or with recording dropped stay opaque as written.

decisions.summary: Kept only when every test of the file passed in a run not filtered by -k, a marker or a node id; a failure removes the entry
decisions.why: FR-013 'a tooling test file that passed' (the whole file) and 'a failure is never kept'.

decisions.summary: Files keyed by git blob id (changed files hashed as git would), interpreter version stored beside; kept in the common dir's l7r-cache
decisions.why: FR-013 'each by its content'; the common dir is what lets a clone's pass serve its land-tooling worktree (SC-010); the interpreter match only makes reuse stricter.

decisions.summary: Directory listings keyed by tracked and untracked entries, ignored entries left out
decisions.why: The literal rule defeats the request's purpose concretely: the worktree land-tooling builds carries none of the clone's ignored artifacts (__pycache__, generated files), so a listing compared with ignored entries never matches clone to worktree and SC-010's own case is unreachable for any test that lists a directory. D16's 'nothing it read is a file git ignores' bounds the file case. Residual seam, recorded: nothing bounds a test whose outcome depends on an ignored entry it lists but never opens.

decisions.summary: Reads of the content caches (.git/l7r-cache/) left out of the recorded inputs
decisions.why: The literal rule defeats the purpose: those cache files are rewritten as entries are added on every run, so any test touching a cached tool would never be reused; each entry is keyed by what it holds, and the caches are held transparent (output identical with cache on and off). Residual seam, recorded: a test asserting on the live common-dir cache's state rather than a tmp cache would be skipped on changed inputs.

decisions.summary: Reuse only under L7R_TEST_DEPS=reuse, set by land-tooling.sh alone
decisions.why: FR-013 'make land-tooling - the one caller, through a named switch its checks set'.

decisions.summary: Deselected only where interpreter matches, nothing opaque, nothing read is git-ignored, every file and directory reads the same; run prints files and tests reused
decisions.why: FR-013 'finds every one of them unchanged, the file is not run again and the run says so'; the extra conditions only make reuse stricter.

decisions.summary: Guard suites keep their own reuse (make hooks-test); measured as m:land-tooling-tests-reuse
decisions.why: FR-013 'The guard suites keep the reuse they have'; the measurement is SC-010's.

decisions.summary: quote-verbatim verdict(passage, page) in a ParseCache named by the module's code sha, keyed by passage and page-text sha256; report compared byte for byte with L7R_CACHE_OFF=1
decisions.why: FR-014: kept by passage and page text under the code version that judged it, report the same with and without the cache (SC-011); the comparison enforces the request.

decisions.summary: audit hook in each worker and a sitecustomize in every child Python note files read and directories listed, written as first seen
decisions.why: FR-013: a file records what it read in its own process and every Python process it started.

decisions.summary: a non-recording program marks the file opaque unless its cwd (and any -C) is outside the repository and no argument names a path inside it; an isolated or unrecorded Python child is opaque
decisions.why: Implements FR-013's 'a file that started any other program against the repository is always run'; it closes the previous round's hole (an outside path no longer exempts a git run in the repository). Read 'inside the repository' as any path whose git common dir is this repository's (the clone, its worktrees), resolved through symlinks, so a linked tree outside the directory counts as inside; a linked tree made outside the test file is a detection gap, not a decision the block makes.

decisions.summary: git init <dir> and git clone <src> <dst> judged by the paths they name
decisions.why: With every named path outside the repository they read nothing of it, so they are not 'against the repository'; a <src> that is this repository or any tree of it names an inside path and is opaque.

decisions.summary: git rev-parse asking only where the repository is is not opaque
decisions.why: FR-013 gives its own reason: always run 'since what that program read is not known'. A location query reads the repository's location, not its content, and reuse is keyed by content under the accepted spec, so the rule's purpose is not touched. Bounded to location options only (--show-toplevel, --git-dir, --absolute-git-dir, --git-common-dir, --show-prefix, --show-cdup, --is-inside-work-tree); any form that resolves a revision or reads refs or config (HEAD, --verify, --abbrev-ref, ...) is outside 'their kind' and opaque.

decisions.summary: sleep, true, false, echo are not opaque
decisions.why: They read nothing of the repository.

decisions.summary: a fully passed, unfiltered file's reads kept by blob id / directory entries / interpreter version; content caches left out; a failure removes the entry
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; FR-013 'each by its content', 'a failure is never kept'.

decisions.summary: L7R_TEST_DEPS=reuse set by land-tooling.sh alone
decisions.why: FR-013: make land-tooling the one caller through a named switch its checks set.

decisions.summary: reuse runs, the gate's -m tooling run and make test-file record passes
decisions.why: Recording in more runs serves FR-013's 'a file the clone passed'. It rests on the premise that -m tooling selects whole files, which D15's 'not filtered by a marker' contradicts as written: the implementation must satisfy D15's 'every test of a file passed' by checking the file's collected tests all ran, not by trusting the marker, and D15's wording should name the whole-file case so the two agree. A conflict between two within decisions, not against the request.

decisions.summary: deselected where interpreter matches, nothing opaque, nothing git-ignored read, every file and directory reads the same; counts printed
decisions.why: FR-013: not run again where every input is unchanged, and the run says so. Figure m:land-tooling-tests-reuse carries its key and command; not re-run under the bundle's read-nothing-in-the-repository rule.

decisions.summary: quote-verbatim verdicts in a ParseCache by code sha, keyed by passage and page sha256; compared with L7R_CACHE_OFF=1
decisions.why: Unchanged since its CLEAR verdict; FR-014.

decisions.summary: A tooling test file's reads recorded by an audit hook in the worker and every Python child; an unrecorded program against the repository makes the file opaque (git init/clone judged by their paths, git rev-parse location queries, sleep/true/false/echo excepted as reading no repository content); a pass is kept by content only when every test of the file ran and passed - none deselected by -k, a marker or a reuse, checked from pytest's deselections, and no node id named; a failure removes the entry.
decisions.why: FR-013 keeps a pass of a FILE; the change only tightens when a pass counts as the file's (a partly deselected file is not a file that passed), so fewer passes are kept, never more, and it lets the gate's -m tooling run record exactly where it ran whole files, which D16 already relied on. Nothing the GM asked to skip is narrowed; the opaque rule and its exceptions are unchanged from the CLEAR text and only exempt programs that read no repository content, which FR-013's 'what that program read is not known' does not reach.

decisions.summary: Reuse switched on by land-tooling alone (L7R_TEST_DEPS=reuse); reuse, gate -m tooling and make test-file runs record; a kept file is skipped when interpreter, opacity, ignored-file and content checks all match; the run prints what it reused; guard suites keep their own reuse.
decisions.why: Unchanged since CLEAR; implements 'skip suites the clone already passed' for the one caller FR-013 names.

decisions.summary: quote-verbatim verdicts kept in a ParseCache named by the module's code sha, keyed by passage and page-text sha256; report compared byte for byte with the cache off.
decisions.why: Unchanged since CLEAR; is FR-014 and the GM's quote-verbatim ask.

decisions.summary: read-only git subcommands with no stdin, no --output and no location variable are questions; answers digested at the end of the run and re-asked once in the worktree; every other git command opaque
decisions.why: Carries FR-015 as written: the exclusions (stdin, --output, GIT_DIR and the other location variables) are FR-015's 'may change the repository, or cannot be asked again', which still make the file run. Asides for the session, not rulings: git status opportunistically refreshes .git/index (no answer changes; GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 would make it literally read-only); blame --contents - reads stdin and is not caught by the --stdin/--batch test; and 'the tests do not write the repository' is the stated, not measured, premise the end-of-run answer rests on.

decisions.summary: the recording's variables put into a Python child's own environment at the Popen audit event; -I/-E/-S children stay opaque; os.open by relative name not a repository read
decisions.why: FR-016 verbatim, including the -I/-E/-S opacity, which is the spec's own words; the relative os.open fix corrects a false .git read and serves FR-015/FR-020's reuse.

decisions.summary: two content-keyed .git caches join CACHE_READS; tooling tests under a fixed SPECIFY_FEATURE; test_makefile_recipe_comments checks tracked Makefiles only; every remaining cause replayed or recorded in R9
decisions.why: FR-020's 'made known or recorded'. The Makefile test's narrower reach is not a loosened check: the stale .claude/worktrees/ copies are not the repository, and the guard's subject is the repository's recipes. The remaining causes are covered by deferral to the each-cause pass, which FR-020 permits (recorded with test-seconds where not reusable).

decisions.summary: land-tooling step timing: prepare, worktree, patch, checks, push; a JSON line per landing; lands first and alone as SC-013's before
decisions.why: FR-017 names the guard suites and the tooling tests as separate steps; D21 collapses them into one 'checks' step. The GM's amendment-2 words are 'figure out where the rest of the 100 or so seconds goes', and the guard suites alone are ~80 s of it (R7, FR-018) - a log reading 'checks N s' cannot say where. The before landing is D21 alone, so SC-013's before would carry one lump, and SC-013's after-proof (the two overlap, their step times in the log) needs each as its own step. Nothing makes separate steps impossible. Fix: D21's step list carries the guard suites and the tooling tests as two 'step <name>' entries, before and after D22 runs them side by side.

decisions.summary: HOOKS_PYTEST_SKIP=tests/tooling/ in a landing; guard suites and tooling tests as two background jobs joined before the push; hooks-test pytest phase loads the reuse plugin
decisions.why: FR-018: each tooling file once, in the run that can reuse, and the two independent checks side by side. The skip is safe on the premise that the tooling run covers all of tests/tooling/; loading the plugin in a clone's own hooks-test is the means by which 'the run that can reuse the clone's pass' has a pass to reuse, so it enforces FR-018 rather than adding behavior.
